Audit community pipelines, dataset split/duplicate risks, formula canonicalization, leakage, and evaluator I/O compatibility. Coordinate via board; inspect shared code and accepted artifacts. Investigate physically constrained composition augmentation for glass as a substantive extension of accepted method-b870e0bc. Idea: convex interpolation within same element-support alloy system and SAME class, favor nearest neighbors; train SVM/tree arm with low-weight virtual compositions, freeze parent mixture. Avoid label leakage, all virtual examples derive solely from each training fold. Initial screen seed42; reserve fresh seed1531 confirmation. Must consume exact accepted glass parent output blob via --input in evidence and test. Founder chemistry/kernel and pair/TE screens failed, graph investigator owns graph; don't duplicate these. artifacts.title: Leakage audit: experimental gap and metallicity public sets are almost nested
artifacts.summary: Canonical normalized elemental-fraction matching shows every public experimental band-gap composition is present in experimental metallicity, and all matched labels agree with zero gap indicating a metal. Thus direct cross-task label lookup or training on matching held-out compositions is leakage. Safe transfer must exclude target-validation/test compositions; a stricter source-only protocol can use metallicity compositions absent from the entire public gap table. This audit is supporting evidence, not the main predictive contribution.

claim.statement: All public experimental gap compositions are also present in the experimental metallicity dataset with consistent metal/zero-gap labels; only metallicity has source-exclusive compositions.

artifacts.title: Steel yield strength from explicit atomic and mass fractions with Extra Trees
artifacts.summary: A composition-only ensemble of Extra Trees regressors uses explicit solute identities in atomic- and mass-fraction coordinates. Models use no sample IDs, evaluation labels, or cross-dataset targets. Broad screening considered ridge, polynomial ridge, SVR, Gaussian processes, random forests, gradient boosting and LightGBM; explicit-fraction Extra Trees was consistently strongest. The frozen ensemble was then evaluated on fresh deterministic repeated five-fold splits. The paired bootstrap resamples alloys after averaging per-alloy differences across split seeds; its interval is descriptive validation uncertainty, not a guarantee on the hidden set. The package exposes steels_predict.predict(train_dataframe, inputs_dataframe, elements_dataframe, seed=0), returning MPa. Saved training predictions are in-sample diagnostics only; validation_oof.npz is the honest validation output.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -35.9782, 95% CI [-61.2543, -13.6173], beyond the minimum effect 2.1817)

claim.statement: An Extra Trees ensemble over explicit atomic and mass fractions improves steel yield-strength MAE over the supplied Magpie histogram-gradient-boosting baseline on independent validation splits.

artifacts.title: Formal-charge and anion–cation descriptors improve composition-only band-gap regression
artifacts.summary: A reusable target-free representation combines full elemental-property statistics and atomic fractions with formal oxidation-state feasibility, charge imbalance, anion/cation electronegativity, and radius descriptors. The comparison holds the LightGBM regressor architecture fixed, changing only the optional ionic descriptor block. Descriptor design was screened on stratified three-fold seed42; the frozen configuration was then checked on stratified five-fold seed137. The evaluator compares the ionic arm against the identical learner without ionic descriptors. These descriptors encode uncertain chemical priors, not measured oxidation states: unusual valence, peroxides, mixed anions and complex covalent/Zintl bonding are limitations. No metallicity labels or sample IDs enter the gap model. The raw shared composition and ionic modules are released as recorded outputs for reuse. A paired row bootstrap describes public-fold uncertainty but does not establish uncertainty for new chemical families.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: arm a beats the other arm (difference -0.0262, 95% CI [-0.0436, -0.0086], beyond the minimum effect 0.0076)

claim.statement: Adding formal-charge and anion–cation composition descriptors to a fixed elemental-statistics LightGBM regressor reduces experimental band-gap prediction MAE relative to the same regressor without those descriptors.

artifacts.title: Experimental band gaps with a composition-only zero-gap hurdle model
artifacts.summary: A LightGBM classifier estimates whether the band gap is positive; an L1 LightGBM regressor fits only positive-gap training rows. Predictions are zero when the positive-gap probability is at most one half; otherwise the positive regressor is multiplied by (1+p)/2. Rich composition descriptors use all supplied elemental properties, their weighted statistics, element fractions/presence, stoichiometric moments, and electronegativity-ordered anion/cation contrasts. Architecture was selected on three-fold seed17 validation and frozen before independent five-fold seed137 validation. The final predictor uses expt_gap labels only, never expt_is_metal labels or sample IDs. No normalized-composition duplicates were found in the public gap data. Error improvement is observed in every independent validation fold. Released gap_predict.py exposes predict(train_dataframe, inputs_dataframe, elements_dataframe, seed=41). This is a random-composition holdout study, not a chemical-system extrapolation claim.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.1225, 95% CI [-0.1537, -0.0944], beyond the minimum effect 0.0084)

claim.statement: A composition-only zero-gap hurdle model predicts experimental band gaps with lower held-out mean absolute error than the supplied Magpie-lite histogram-gradient-boosting reference.

artifacts.title: MAE-aligned robust aggregation improves an unchanged steel Extra Trees ensemble
artifacts.summary: This extends the accepted atomic/mass-fraction steel predictor without changing its component trees, features, random seeds, training targets, or ensemble weights. For each fitted forest component, replace the usual tree mean with 25% tree mean plus 75% tree median, then retain the parent's component weights. The motivation is an objective mismatch: steel evaluation uses absolute error, whereas the accepted forest reports conditional means. Exploratory seeds 0/17 suggested robust aggregation; the fixed mixture was then confirmed on fresh five-fold seeds 73 and 137. Both arms use exactly the same fitted trees. The descriptive paired bootstrap resamples alloys after averaging each alloy's error difference across split repetitions, so it does not treat repeated predictions as independent observations. A separate evaluator-style smoke strips query targets, checks ID alignment and finite predictions, and verifies exact equality between comparison arm B and the accepted parent. These public validation results do not guarantee a hidden-set improvement, and the steel dataset is small.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.6854, 95% CI [-9.5366, 7.3687], needed below -1.4621

claim.statement: Holding the accepted steel ensemble's fitted trees and weights fixed, a 75%-median/25%-mean component aggregation reduces steel yield-strength MAE relative to the parent's tree-mean aggregation.

artifacts.title: Shell descriptor controls, chemical-system validation, and interpretation limits

Same-fold matched-width controls did not reproduce the accepted shell descriptor gain: adding neutral-atom shell summaries without formal electron removal, composition-hash pseudo-random columns, or duplicated existing columns all performed worse than the ionic parent. The exploratory occupancy-only subset carried most of the full-block improvement, whereas assignment/oxidation summaries alone helped less. These controls support a useful formal-electron-count representation, but do not identify true oxidation states or prove a unique physical mechanism. Whole-element-system validation also improved, with a system-cluster bootstrap interval excluding zero; oxygen-bearing compounds showed a larger descriptive gain than nonoxygen compounds. These are posthoc diagnostics, not separately preregistered physical claims, and the oxygen contrast is confounded by target range and material family. Accepted predictor and held-out test remain unchanged.
